title: Preface
summary: A 1967 CIA dispatch (Approved for Release 2025/12/29) addresses public criticism of the Warren Commission report on JFK's assassination. It notes growing speculation about conspiracy and a poll showing most Americans doubt Oswald acted alone, and warns that doubts about the Commission harm U.S. government reputation and implicate the organization. Guidance: avoid initiating discussion, but where it exists, use liaison and elite contacts and propaganda assets to rebut critics, citing the Commission's thoroughness, critics' biases, implausibility of conspiracy, Oswald's unsuitability, and explanations for alleged 'mysterious deaths.' Encourages citing the Report itself and attaches unclassified background materials.

title: Background Survey of Books Concerning theAssassination of President Kennedy
summary: A 1967 CIA background survey of books on the Kennedy assassination critiques critics of the Warren Commission. It covers authors such as Joesten, Lane, Sauvage, and Epstein, noting their prior conspiracy claims, left-wing or Communist ties, and profit motives. It cites Lane's research and tactics, Epstein's factual errors, and Popkin's theories, plus Garson's parody. It also covers the media reception, upcoming books, and Soviet-bloc propaganda amplifying the critiques.

title: H D. m

nodes.title: H D. m (intro)
nodes.summary: Spectator discusses Edward Jay Epstein's book Inquest critiquing the Warren Commission. Epstein argues Kennedy and Connally were hit by separate bullets, implying two assassins, based on Zapruder film timing versus the 2.3-second bolt cycle of Oswald's rifle. He cites FBI reports of a back wound with no exit, contradicting the official autopsy, and implies the Commission altered or forged evidence. The article notes the autopsy was revised after the Dallas tracheostomy neck wound was learned of, and that Epstein's Esquire piece presses for release of autopsy photos, which the Kennedy family resists.

nodes.title: 1. E275-tein's thesis that if the President and the Governor by the same bullet, there must have been two assassins:
1. E275-tein's thesis that if the President and the Governor by the same bullet, there must have been two assassins: (intro)
nodes.summary: Discusses Epstein's thesis that if President Kennedy and Governor Connally were hit by the same bullet, there must have been two assassins. The Commission thought the men were probably hit by one bullet but could not fully exclude separate hits, since the Zapruder film is two-dimensional and obscured during a key period, and an oak tree may have blocked the view. Connally's testimony that he heard a first shot is consistent with a missed first shot. All shots were attributed to the sixth-floor window, supported by the rifle, cartridge cases, and witness consensus of three shots; Epstein's counter-witnesses are weak. The Commission was not predetermined and refused to build conclusions on debatable evidence.

nodes.title: 2. Epstein’s thesis that either the FBI's reports (that the bullet entering the President's back did not exit) were wrong, or the official autopsy report was falsified.
nodes.summary: The text is a scanned, OCR-garbled 1966 critique of Edward Jay Epstein's book Inquest on the Warren Commission. It covers: (1) Epstein's claim that the FBI autopsy reports were accurate and the official autopsy was falsified, countered by the late delivery of the doctors' report to the FBI and Hoover's 1966 explanation; (2) the shirt and coat holes, explained by the President waving; (3) the wound's location, supported by Commander Boswell's measurements and the autopsy films; (4) implausibility of a conspiracy and falsification; (5) Mark Lane's Ruby testimony and Trevor-Roper's critique of Lane; and (6) an Arnold Fein article arguing critics of the Warren Report failed to meet evidentiary standards, while the Commission also had flaws.

Covers Epstein's thesis that if Kennedy and Connally were hit by one bullet, there were two assassins. The Commission judged one bullet likely but could not fully exclude separate hits, given the two-dimensional, partly obscured Zapruder film and an oak tree; Connally's heard first shot fits a missed shot. All shots are attributed to the sixth-floor window, supported by rifle, cartridges and witnesses. Epstein's counter-witnesses are weak; the Commission was not predetermined. Also a garbled 1966 critique of Epstein's Inquest: autopsy reports, shirt holes, wound location, Lane's Ruby testimony, and Fein's evidentiary-standards argument.

nodes.title: Chapter VI of the Report proper,
nodes.summary: A scanned, OCR-garbled excerpt from the Warren Commission Report's Chapter VI on the conspiracy investigation. It critiques books by Weisberg, Lane, Epstein, Popkin, Sauvage and Fox that challenge the autopsy findings. Key points: the autopsy doctors' report (Humes, Boswell, Finck) versus FBI agents' Sibert and O'Neill reports on wound locations and bullet trajectories; the single-bullet theory and Connally's wounds; alleged alteration of the autopsy report; Marina Oswald and Helen Markham's credibility; the Commission's use of evidence and witnesses; and alleged second assassins or plots. The text also includes a newspaper-style piece on Epstein's claims about the jacket measurements and the Boswell sketch, with Dr. Boswell disputing him.

It says the Commission may have altered evidence and that the autopsy was revised after the Dallas neck wound was learned of, and it notes Epstein's push for autopsy photo release. The excerpt also covers Chapter VI critiques of Weisberg, Lane, Popkin and others, autopsy versus FBI report conflicts, the single-bullet theory, witness credibility, and Boswell's dispute.

nodes.summary: A scanned, OCR-garbled multi-page excerpt (declassified, approved for release 2025/12/29) on the Warren Commission and JFK assassination. It covers critics' theories (second assassin, double Oswald, CIA/FBI involvement) and the Commission's findings: a single lone assassin firing three shots from the sixth-floor window, with no credible grassy-knoll shots. It discusses the autopsy report discrepancies (FBI December 9 report vs. official autopsy), the 'magic bullet' and Connally's wounds, and Oswald's marksmanship and rifle. It also covers Edward Epstein's book 'Inquest' and reviews by Revere, Kempton, and Weisberg, the Rowland testimony dispute, and an Arlen Specter interview defending the investigation.

nodes.title: Not Quite as Shrill
nodes.summary: A scanned, OCR-garbled 1960s-era essay (approved for release 2025/12/29) reviews assassination literature on President Kennedy's death. It criticizes the Warren Commission report as thorough-seeming but flawed, and discusses critics Edward Jay Epstein, Richard Popkin, Mark Lane ("Rush to Judgment"), Harold Weisberg, and Hugh Trevor-Roper. It notes the single-assassin conclusion, the magic-bullet and multiple-shot debates, and the skepticism spreading in Britain and Europe, and argues that doubt should be followed by a fair hearing of both sides.

title: does
summary: The text is a garbled OCR scan of a 1960s essay (apparently by Richard Hofstadter-era commentary, reprinted with Warren Commission materials) defending the Warren Report on JFK's assassination. It argues that critics' conspiracy theories are speculative and that a single-assassin conclusion is reasonable, while warning against hysteria and the dangers of conspiracy-minded thinking. It discusses the 'single bullet' theory, Oswald's ties, and critics like Mark Lane, Epstein, and Weisberg. It also includes a Q&A with a Warren Commission member defending the investigation's independence, methods, and the case against reopening it. Much of the text is unreadable OCR noise.
